text:
Broad Street Hockey ran it as a headline last week: Jamie Drysdale is finally becoming the defenseman the Flyers envisioned. The numbers back the point production. He has 16 points in 28 games, six on the power play, at 1.51 points per 60 against a league average of 1.11 for defensemen, while playing 22.6 minutes a night.

The signature moment came November 19 in Ottawa, when his late third-period goal finished a comeback from three down in a game Philadelphia won 6-5. That's the version of Drysdale the Flyers traded for: fast (93rd percentile top speed by NHL EDGE) and willing to join the rush.

The other half of his game is more complicated. Philadelphia gets just 41.5% of the five-on-five shot attempts with him on the ice, and his relative numbers are negative. Evolving-Hockey had him 109th among 215 defensemen last season, about league average. He's also blocking a lot of shots (46), which is what happens when the other team has the puck. His ice time dropped to 16.2 minutes against Vancouver on Friday, his lightest of the month, which is the thing to watch next.
